summary.intent: Plan and execute CipherBox Phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation consolidation + batch/drag move parity), run standard PR-QA (simplify, security reviews, CodeRabbit CLI, push, PR, resolve GitHub review), fix resulting CI E2E failures, then run verify-phase on phases 47–49 and mark them complete.
summary.outcome: PR #509 merged to main with 5 plans/6 requirements including scope-expanded batch+drag parity; two architectural improvements bundled in (write-key distribution for write-shares on subtree descendants; decentralized signature-gated IPNS cache keyed by name not user); all CI E2E failures diagnosed and fixed; phases 47–49 verified (17+4+24 truths each, adversarially confirmed with 0 overturns) and marked Complete, bringing the project to 25/34 phases (74%).

repo: `collectChildKeys` in `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts` historically emitted only read keys (`folder`/`file`) for share descendants even on write-permission shares — recipients could never move into owner-created subfolders. Fixed by adding a `permission` param and emitting `folder-ipns`/`file-ipns` on write shares, guarded on the optional `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` field.

CipherBox resolves IPNS via a DB cache (`folder_ipns` table) that is the authoritative source — the DHT is a secondary fallback. The table was keyed `(userId, ipnsName)` causing non-owners to fork duplicate rows on publish. Re-architected to `(ipnsName)` alone with mandatory Ed25519 signature verification, making authority a function of key possession. Revocation now requires IPNS key rotation instead of a server-side revoke.

`SharedFileBrowser` gated `SelectionActionBar` on `selectedIds.size > 0` — the first click of a double-click selected one item, the bar rendered above the file list, shifted rows down, and the second click missed its target, silently breaking all double-click folder navigation. Private vault `FileBrowser.tsx:205` correctly uses `size > 1`.

`SharedFolderRow` renders folder names with a trailing `/` in `.file-name` text content. E2E `getFolderItemNames()` must strip the slash; other pre-existing specs use `.includes()` for the same reason.

The desktop E2E conflict-detection helpers (`test-conflict-detection.sh` / `.ps1`) faked a competing device by POSTing a dummy unsigned byte string to `/ipns/publish`. Under the new signature-gated server this is correctly rejected (400). The `.sh` only logged a warning (macOS/Linux passed falsely); the `.ps1` `throw`s on failure (Windows broke). Fixed with `bump-ipns-sequence.mjs` that publishes a real validly-signed record at sequence+1.

`FolderEntry.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` is typed required (`packages/core/src/folder/types.ts:40`) while `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` is optional (`file/types.ts:68`). The `collectChildKeys` folder branch accessed it unconditionally; a defensive null guard was added to degrade gracefully on malformed legacy metadata rather than crash.

`ChildKeyDtoKeyType` in the API DTO was missing `folder-ipns` (only `file`/`folder`/`file-ipns`). `CHILD_KEY_TYPES` is the single source of truth feeding both `@IsIn` validation and `@ApiProperty enum`, so adding it there propagated everywhere including the regenerated client.

GSD `phase uat-passed <N>` is listed in CLI help but has no handler — use `phase complete <N>` instead. The `phase complete` command also emits a false-positive 'needs human verification' warning when `previous_status: human_needed` appears in VERIFICATION.md frontmatter history (regex matches the history line, not the current status).
Release-please bumps crate `Cargo.toml` version fields but never regenerates `Cargo.lock`, leaving the lockfile stale after every Rust release. Captured as a pending todo.

The `ipns` npm package (`ipns@10.1.3`) is already a dependency of `@cipherbox/core` (and transitively the API via `@cipherbox/crypto`). `validate` from `ipns/validator`, `unmarshalIPNSRecord`, and `extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord` were available for server-side verification without adding deps.

`extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord` returns `undefined` synchronously (not a rejected promise) for identity-key records that omit the embedded public key. Wrapping the call in try/catch rather than `.catch()` is the correct handling pattern.

GSD executor agents report `commit_failed` as a false negative in non-worktree sequential mode — the commits actually land. Always verify with `git log` rather than trusting the executor's reported commit status.

The `check-api-client.sh` pre-commit hook requires the generated client to be staged whenever `.dto.ts`/`.controller.ts`/`.entity.ts` files are changed AND generated files have unstaged changes. Regenerating the client (openapi-generator) triggered a version header bump (0.39.0→0.40.0) across 131 files — benign but noisy in diffs.

CodeRabbit under the CHILL profile delivers review-body nitpicks rather than inline review threads. `/resolve-pr-reviews` queries GraphQL `reviewThreads` and finds 0 threads, masking the body-bundled nitpicks. Must also fetch review bodies separately to triage bundled comments.

code.finding: Private vault gates SelectionActionBar on `selectedIds.size > 1`, not `> 0` — this prevents the bar from appearing on a plain single click (which is also the first click of a double-click), avoiding a layout shift that would break double-click navigation.

TypeScript 4.4+ narrows a union type through `const isFolder = item.type === 'folder'` (aliased discriminant), so subsequent accesses like `item.ipnsName` at line 149 are type-safe without an explicit type guard — `tsc -b` confirms no error.

`findActiveWriteShare` was an exact `ipnsName` match against top-level write Share rows only — no descendant coverage. Non-owner publishes for any descendant ipnsName fell through to the create-new path at line 287, forking a duplicate recipient-owned row. This was the M-1 server authorization gap.

Changed `@Unique(['userId', 'ipnsName'])` to `@Unique(['ipnsName'])` — one canonical record per IPNS name, authority determined by Ed25519 signature rather than user ownership. `userId` retained as denormalized creator marker for TEE enrollment and cleanup only.

`collectChildKeys` folder branch accessed `folder.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` unconditionally. Unlike `FilePointer`, `FolderEntry.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` is typed required, so it can't be undefined for type-conforming data — but a defensive null guard was added for malformed legacy IPFS metadata.

`enumerateSharedSubtree` writability check requires a per-subfolder `share_keys` row with `keyType: 'folder-ipns'`. Before write-key distribution was fixed, recipients never got these rows for owner-created subfolders, so all owner-created subfolders appeared read-only (`writable: false`) in the move dialog.

`onMoveItemTo` closure was routing by the *drop target folder's* selection state and discarding the dragged payload — dragging an unselected item while others were selected moved the wrong items. Fixed to resolve dragged items from `sortedChildren` via the forwarded `DragItem[]` from `SharedFolderRow`.

Hand-rolled IPNS record parser (162 lines) was deleted and replaced with `ipns` library calls (`unmarshalIPNSRecord`, `extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord`) now in `@cipherbox/crypto`. The hand-rolled version duplicated library behavior and skipped signature validation entirely.

New `verifyIpnsRecordSignature(ipnsName, marshalledRecord)` helper: parses ipnsName as base36 CID → peerIdFromCID → `validate(peerId.publicKey, record)` from `ipns/validator`. Returns false on any error or null public key rather than throwing.

workflow: Run GSD executors sequentially in wave order (not parallel worktrees) for AFK/autonomous runs — avoids worktree merge-base footguns and concurrent test-suite RAM starvation. The SDK dist must be manually rebuilt between waves when new public API methods are added, since web `tsc -b` checks the built dist, not source.

CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit review --agent`) returns structured JSON findings with schema `{severity, fileName, codegenInstructions, suggestions}`. The GitHub review posts findings in the review body (not inline threads) under the CHILL profile — `/resolve-pr-reviews` must also fetch review bodies to surface bundled nitpicks.

When a background `gh run watch` or poll script uses `status` as a variable name in zsh, it conflicts with zsh's read-only `$status` variable and fails with exit code 1. Use a different variable name (e.g., `run_status`).

ci-e2e workflow dispatch via `gh workflow run` can return a network timeout error even when the dispatch succeeds — always verify with `gh run list` after a timeout rather than assuming failure and retrying.

The GSD plan-checker runs as a separate verification agent after the planner and is worth the iteration cost — it caught a REQ-3 unit-test gap (vacuous pass in plan 49-03) that needed a targeted planner revision before execution.

For exhaustive phase verification, running 3 parallel `gsd-verifier` agents each followed by an independent adversarial skeptic via Workflow tool (6 agents total) with pre-run behavioral test evidence injected as context is faster and more thorough than sequential single-pass verification.

The GSD `gsd:stats` workflow reports `Needs Review` for phases that have been executed but not yet verified, and `Executed` for older phases without verification artifacts at all — these are separate states with different remediation paths.

When checking whether CI E2E failures are regressions vs pre-existing flakes, compare against `gh run list --branch main` — a green main history over 8+ runs reliably distinguishes regressions from flakes.

friction: AFK commit-signing disable (`git config --local commit.gpgsign false`) left all branch commits unsigned; the repo enforces signed commits on PRs, requiring a signed rebase or admin override at merge time.

GSD executor agents report `commit_failed` as a false negative in sequential non-worktree mode — multiple commits in the session appeared failed but had actually landed, requiring manual `git log` verification each time.

The `gsd-tools` parser deletions were already staged from a prior `git rm` when the write-key distribution commit ran, sweeping them into commit `1be0dca11` and making that commit non-building in isolation (the parser-consuming API service was committed in the next commit). CI-only-runs-on-HEAD mitigated this, but it's a footgun.
`phase uat-passed <N>` is listed in `gsd-tools` CLI help output but has no implementation — silently fails with a usage error. Only `phase complete` is implemented.
zsh `$status` is a read-only built-in variable; a background watch script using `status` as a loop variable failed with exit code 1, requiring a restart with a renamed variable.
CodeRabbit's CHILL profile doesn't auto-re-review incremental pushes, so verifying that nitpick fixes satisfied the review required a second manual poll rather than an automatic re-check.

The `check-api-client.sh` pre-commit hook swept 131 generated files (an OpenAPI version header bump) into the commit whenever any DTO changed — makes it hard to isolate the meaningful semantic change in the diff.

API TypeScript has 3 pre-existing errors in untouched spec files (`itemNameEncrypted`, `@nestjs/common` type) that block `tsc --project tsconfig.json` but not `nest build` — the gap between type-check commands causes confusion about what 'passing typecheck' means for the API.

`gsd-tools phase complete` emits a spurious 'needs human verification' warning for phases whose VERIFICATION.md frontmatter contains `previous_status: human_needed` in the history section — the status regex matches the history line, not the current status field.
open_items: Write access to shared folder subtrees is now revocable only via IPNS key rotation + re-share (not server-side). This is an accepted architectural tradeoff for decentralization but must be documented in the share/revoke UX and future key-rotation tooling.

Full SDK-level subtree cycle guard for `moveInSharedFolder`: current guard is UI (descendant picker exclusion) + SDK self-move throw, but a malicious/crafted client could still call the op directly to create a tree cycle affecting co-recipients. Documented in PR as optional hardening.
Client-side IPNS `signatureVerified` enforcement on resolution — the client currently trusts the server-returned record without verifying the signature client-side. Noted in PR as a fast-follow.
Un-cached-name IPNS resolve verification — records resolved by name-only lookup have no signature check on the client side. Noted in PR.
